title: Forward Exchange Coordination
name: Forward Exchange Coordination
metaTitle: Forward Exchange Coordination in San Diego, CA
metaDescription: Forward exchange coordination for San Diego owners selling first and buying replacement property second, with the market work included alongside the paperwork.

sections.html: A forward exchange is the ordinary sequence, sell the relinquished property first, then acquire a replacement within 180 days, and it is the structure behind most San Diego 1031s. The mechanics sound simple on a diagram. Running one against San Diego's actual market, tight industrial supply, biotech and life-science demand near Torrey Pines and UTC, and tourism-driven retail, is where a coordination package earns its fee or does not.

sections.heading: The Gap Between "Coordination" and Actually Sourcing Property
sections.html: Plenty of forward-exchange packages describe themselves as full coordination while actually covering only the paperwork side, the exchange agreement, the identification letter, the QI liaison work, and leaving the investor to find replacement property entirely on their own. That is a real service, but it is not the same as coordination that includes screening candidates in the port-adjacent industrial corridor or a Sorrento Valley lab building. Ask specifically whether property sourcing is included or billed separately before comparing quotes.

sections.heading: What Full Coordination Actually Involves in San Diego
sections.html: Beyond the exchange documents themselves, coordinating a San Diego forward exchange means tracking lender preflight items against the closing calendar, screening replacement candidates for financing feasibility, and keeping the qualified intermediary's paperwork moving in step with both the relinquished-side closing and the replacement-side purchase. Each of those pieces has its own timeline, and they do not automatically stay aligned without someone actively managing all three.

sections.heading: Where San Diego's Market Adds Real Friction
sections.html: Otay Mesa border-industrial deals can involve customs and foreign-trade-zone considerations that have nothing to do with the exchange itself but still affect closing timing. Tourism-driven retail near the coast carries seasonal lease and revenue patterns that change how a replacement property should be underwritten. Biotech and life-science tenants near UTC often carry longer lead times for lease assignment and consent. None of this shows up in a generic forward-exchange checklist built for a market with none of these dynamics.

sections.heading: The Coordination Checklist We Run Start to Finish
sections.html:
Every San Diego forward exchange we coordinate covers the same core items, in sequence:

  • Exchange agreement and qualified intermediary setup before the relinquished-property closing
  • Replacement property screening against financing and title feasibility
  • 45-day identification letter, filed under the rule that fits the deal
  • Lender preflight coordination on the replacement purchase
  • Closing sequencing across both properties against the 180-day deadline

sections.heading: What Stays With Your Other Advisors
sections.html: Coordination does not replace your qualified intermediary, who holds funds and issues the required certifications, or your tax advisor, who confirms the final reporting position. Our job is keeping every moving piece, paperwork, financing, and closing timing, aligned so those advisors get accurate information at the right time.

sections.heading: How to Tell a Thin Coordination Package From a Complete One
sections.html:
A thin package usually shows up as a short list of deliverables tied entirely to the exchange documents, with language like "we handle the paperwork" standing in for a detailed scope. A complete package spells out who screens replacement candidates, who tracks the lender's conditions, and who owns the weekly reconciliation between the two closing calendars.

If a provider cannot answer specifically who does what across financing, sourcing, and documentation on a San Diego forward exchange, that gap is usually where the investor ends up doing the work themselves mid-exchange, after already paying for coordination.

Getting a straight answer up front, in writing if possible, is worth more than a polished proposal document, since the proposal rarely gets revisited once the engagement begins and the actual scope becomes whatever gets delivered.

A short list of specific deliverables, screened candidates, tracked lender conditions, weekly closing reconciliation, is worth more upfront clarity than a longer document full of general language about a smooth, coordinated process.

If a provider hesitates to put a specific deliverable list in writing before the engagement starts, that hesitation is itself useful information about how the coordination is likely to unfold once the exchange is underway.

Investors comparing quotes across San Diego providers are usually better served treating the deliverable list, not the price alone, as the main point of comparison, since two similarly priced quotes can represent very different amounts of actual work.

That comparison is what actually reveals which quote reflects a genuine market rate for the work involved and which one is priced low because the scope has been quietly narrowed to just the paperwork.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a forward exchange and a reverse exchange?
faqs.a: In a forward exchange, the relinquished property sells before the replacement property is acquired. In a reverse exchange, the replacement is acquired first, which requires an exchange accommodation titleholder to hold it temporarily.

faqs.q: Does forward exchange coordination include finding replacement property?
faqs.a: It should, but not every package includes it. Ask directly whether property screening and sourcing are part of the coordination fee or billed as a separate service.

faqs.q: How does San Diego's market change what coordination needs to cover?
faqs.a: Border-adjacent industrial deals, biotech lease assignment timelines, and seasonal tourism retail patterns all add steps that a generic forward-exchange checklist built for a different market would miss.

faqs.q: Who actually holds the exchange funds during a forward exchange?
faqs.a: The qualified intermediary, from the relinquished-property closing until the replacement purchase closes. The investor never has direct access to the funds during that period.

faqs.q: What happens if a replacement property falls through late in a forward exchange?
faqs.a: A genuinely vetted backup identified property is what prevents this from becoming a failed exchange. If nothing closes by day 180, the deferred gain becomes taxable for the year of sale.
